newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar closes lower, buying on dips tipped.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar closes lower, buying on dips tipped.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar drifted lower during the day to close at US$0.6997/04 from its 0.7008/15 opening.
Dealers said there was buying on any dips and selling capping the kiwi at 0.7020-30.
Offshore interest was dominating trading with no apparent concern at a Trade Weighted Index of 66.55 against the Reserve Bank's assumption of 65 in its economic projections released last week.
"I would be surprised to see the Reserve Bank saying anything so close to the election," one dealer said.
"They would be on a hiding to nothing. After the election, if National wins, they may say 'OK today we have got to do something'."
He said the kiwi was likely to trade in a range from 0.6990 to 0.7020 or 0.6980 to 0.7030 "on the wide" overnight.
Tomorrow's National Business Review-Consultus poll would make "no difference".
"We are still three weeks out from the election. Compare that with the 1993 election when the (ruling) National Party was going to win by ten seats and we got a hung parliament."
